label: GPT-6 Luna
output:
Hi Tolu, I’m Amaka_Bio100. I’m in Biology 100L now, and Medicine was what I applied for too. I scored 251 in JAMB in 2025, applied for Medicine and Surgery, and got offered Biology at a federal university here in Lagos. So I know how disorienting it can feel to see a different course on the portal from the one you’d been hoping for.

The day I saw Biology, I locked myself in my cousin’s room in Surulere and cried. I didn’t even eat. My mum kept telling people at church that I was studying Medicine for about two months, and I eventually had to beg her to stop. I’m telling you that because you’re not being dramatic or ungrateful for feeling upset. You had a plan, and now you have a difficult decision to make.

Here’s the honest gist about transferring: it is possible, but it isn’t automatic, and I wouldn’t accept Biology solely because you’ve been promised you can switch to Medicine later. Our level adviser told us that, for our school, you need at least a 4.5 CGPA out of 5.0, and there also has to be a space in Medicine. She said that last year about six students transferred in from the whole faculty, while she thought more than 40 had applied. She also said you need to meet the Medicine cut-offs for both JAMB and post-UTME. I don’t know your school’s cut-offs or your post-UTME score, so your JAMB score of 268 alone doesn’t tell us whether you’d qualify.

Please check the exact rules for your own school with the faculty or department. Ask about the required CGPA, JAMB and post-UTME cut-offs, available spaces, and how the process works. Don’t rely only on forum replies—including mine—because rules differ, and things can change. Your dad may mean well, but “just transfer after first year” leaves out a lot.

I’m still trying to see whether I can qualify. After my first semester, my CGPA is 4.31, which is below the 4.5 our adviser mentioned. I’m working at it, but I can’t promise I’ll get there or that a space will be available even if I do. So Kingsley is wrong to say transfer is a myth, but Favour’s “just read hard” makes it sound much simpler and more certain than it is.

First year isn’t a walk in the park either. We take BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST courses. Physics and Maths are the ones giving people a hard time. There are also practical costs to think about: my lab coat was ₦6,500, my dissecting kit was ₦9,000, and the practical manual was extra. It’s worth asking the department what you’ll need to pay for, so you have the full picture.

But Biology isn’t a bad course. I went into it disappointed, and I’ve ended up enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I expected. During our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted; I was fine. That day I realised I actually liked this kind of work. That doesn’t mean you have to love Biology, or that enjoying it will erase your original goal. It just means your experience might surprise you.

I also want to be honest that rewriting JAMB isn’t a foolish choice if Medicine is still what you want and you’re ready to prepare and try again. A former secondary-school classmate of mine, Ifeoma, rejected a Pharmacy offer to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and is still at home. I’m not sharing that to scare you or say you’ll have the same outcome; I don’t know how her attempts went. I just don’t want to pretend rewriting guarantees Medicine either. Staying home can be hard, but choosing to rewrite is not wrong if you’ve thought about the risks and are prepared for another attempt.

Before you decide, try to separate what *you* want from what your family wants for you. Do you want to study Medicine, or do you mainly feel pressure to become a “doctor” for your parents? And if you accept Biology, would you be willing to study it if a transfer never happened? There’s no shame in answering either question honestly.

Whatever you choose, this isn’t the end of the world. You don’t have to accept Biology just because someone says transfer is easy, and you don’t have to rewrite just because someone says transfer is impossible. Get the real rules from your faculty, think through both paths, and give yourself room to make the decision that fits you.
